VM3 - Write Variables (DBL).vi

Owning Palette: R/W Multiple Variables

Writes multiple VarMan variables of the DBL Number data type.

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle specifies the handle of the Variable Context in which the target variables exist. To operate on global variables, pass -1 to this input. This input is ignored for any element in the name_specs array that refers to a variable by an alias.
name_specs defines the name specifiers of the target variables. Usually, a name specifier is merely a variable name; however, additional options are available. See the Referring to variables topic for details.
values in specifies the variable values to be written. This array must have the same size as name_specs.
writer IDs specifies the Writer IDs for the respective elements in name_specs and values. If the size of this array is less than the size of name_specs, its first element is bound to all values. If this array is empty, zero (0) is used.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
atomic (F) guarantees, if TRUE, that the operation on all variables is executed in a single, atomic transaction. This prevents other VIs or threads from modifying the variables during execution.
dup name_specs is a flow-through parameter with the same value as name_specs.
stats returns additional information about the variable values. Each element of this array is a cluster with the following members:
writer ID indicates the Writer ID for the most recent value.
write MS indicates the Milliseconds Timer value (the output of the Tick Count (ms) primitive) when the variable value was written.
write TS indicates the time stamp (DBL representation), in the universal LabVIEW date/time format, when the variable value was written.
write Cnt indicates the variable write counter. This counter starts at zero (0) when the variable is created and increments every time the variable is written.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains VarMan VI error code identifying an error if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source contains the error description and VI location information if an error occurred.
errCodes returns VarMan Engine error codes individually for each variable. If any element in this array is non-zero, the error out cluster returns the corresponding error description.
